title: unique case Violation on Concurrent One-Hot Bits
bug_signature: VCS-ERROR: unique case violation — state[0]=1 and state[7]=1 simultaneously; next_state=X
rtl:
always_comb begin
  unique case (1'b1)
    state[0]: next_state = S1;  // Violation if state[0] and state[7] both set
    state[7]: next_state = S2;
  endcase
end
expected_root_cause: The unique case construct requires exactly one branch to match; when a one-hot encoding error causes state[0] and state[7] to be simultaneously set, the unique violation fires and next_state becomes X rather than falling through to a safe priority-encoded result.
description: A one-hot state register with a functional error can briefly have two bits set simultaneously; unique case fires a runtime violation and produces undefined next_state rather than resolving by priority.
failure_log: VCS-ERROR: unique case violation — state[0]=1 and state[7]=1 simultaneously; next_state=X
success_log: priority case: first matching branch selected for all state values including multi-hot. No violation.
